transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hi, nice to meet you too. Well, what brings me in is that I just keep getting up when I'm supposed to stay put. It's becoming a bit of a problem. 

Like, during client interviews for my work, or when I'm doing tutoring sessions... even just sitting at my book club. I just can't seem to stay in my chair. People are definitely starting to notice that I can't just sit and listen to them without needing to get up.
When you have to get up, do you feel an inner sense of restlessness or agitation in your body?

I don't think so. I haven't really noticed any kind of inner agitation or restlessness like that. I just... I just get up. It's not really a feeling of being physically uncomfortable or agitated, I just kind of do it.
Did this difficulty staying seated start back when you were a child?

Yeah, it definitely did. My grade-school report cards always said I was bright, but that I just couldn't stay in my seat or wait my turn. My mother actually still jokes about it... she says I treated every classroom like a crime scene that I had to pace through.
Do you often have trouble sustaining your attention on tasks or conversations?

No, not really. I don't have an issue with that. I can focus on my work and follow conversations just fine, I just do a lot of it while standing up or pacing around. The attention part isn't really the problem for me.

latest_inference.note: Childhood-onset persistent inability to remain seated and difficulty waiting turn strongly supports ADHD; intact sustained attention does not rule it out. Lack of inner restlessness argues against akathisia/substance-related causes, and absence of psychotic or mood symptoms makes F31.1, F25.0, and F20.0 unlikely. GAD is not supported by current symptoms.
